answer: Each agent can act freely at first, but earning influence requires a time-locked stake: a zephyr in a haven may post claims, yet cannot steer the market until its deposit has survived several settlement rounds. If a Sybil operator splits funds among a thousand identities, every identity still needs its own locked stake, multiplying the capital tied up and exposing it to slashing when proven to coordinate fraudulently. The inlet is that stake can be returned after honest participation, so the defense taxes attacks rather than demanding permanent permission.
